section_title: How should Timothy’s life support what he teaches?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 11 Command and teach these things. 12 Let no one despise your youth, but set an example for the believers in speech, in conduct, in love, in faith, in purity. 13 Until I come, devote yourself to the public reading of Scripture, to exhortation, and to teaching.

14 Do not neglect the gift that is in you, which was given you through the prophecy spoken over you at the laying on of the hands of the elders. 15 Be diligent in these matters and absorbed in them, so that your progress will be evident to all. 16 Pay close attention to your life and to your teaching. Persevere in these things, for by so doing you will save both yourself and those who hear you.

context_lines: Paul tells Timothy to command and teach these things. His youth is to be answered through an example in speech, conduct, love, faith and purity. The way he lives must support the instruction he gives.
His work includes public reading of Scripture, exhortation and teaching. He is also to use the gift connected with the prophecy over him and the laying on of the elders’ hands.

Paul calls for diligence and visible progress. Timothy must attend both to his life and his teaching and persevere. The closing statement gives this work its weight: his faithful ministry concerns both himself and the people hearing him.
The paragraph combines dependence on God’s gift with careful practice. God’s gift and the elders’ recognition lead into ongoing service and a life that reflects the message.
common_interpretation_lines: Christians commonly understand this as a call for a teacher’s conduct, use of gifts and perseverance to match the message. [Calvin’s comment on verse 16](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/calvin/1_timothy/4.htm) understands the saving language as God using faithful gospel ministry to bring people to Christ. He expressly identifies God as the source of salvation, with human ministers serving as His instruments.

Churches describe the laying on of hands in different ways. The Catholic [Catechism, paragraph 1556](https://www.vatican.va/content/catechism/en/part_two/section_two/chapter_three/article_6/iii_the_three_degrees_of_the_sacrament_of_holy_orders.index.html), describes the Spirit’s gift being passed on through the laying on of hands in ordained succession. The Baptist [1689 Confession, 26.9](https://www.the1689confession.com/1689/chapter-26), describes the church setting apart a person already fitted and gifted by the Spirit. These are the traditions’ own accounts of the practice, rather than an assumption that everyone describes Timothy’s gift and recognition identically.
god_plan_lines: [Romans 10:13–17](https://biblehub.com/bsb/romans/10.htm) connects people calling on the Lord with hearing the message through those sent to preach it. Faithful teaching serves God’s saving mission by making Christ known.

[Ephesians 4:11–16](https://biblehub.com/bsb/ephesians/4.htm) places teachers and other gifts within the growth of the whole body toward maturity in Christ. Timothy’s attention to both life and teaching serves that larger purpose: people equipped to live and grow together in Him.
current_position_lines: We don't have a position on this passage yet. When our study reaches a conclusion the text supports, it will appear here.
